ankle.amac: Opens up the forward bend of the ankle (dorsiflexion). If your ankle is restricted, the load in landings and squats can shift to the knee; this drill prepares the ankle before jumping and squatting.
ipuclari: Place your front foot a hand's width from the wall, toes pointing at the wall.
Keeping your heel pressed into the floor, drive your knee toward the wall.
Track your knee in line with your second and third toes.
If you touch easily, move your foot back a little; if you can't reach, move it closer.
Hold forward for 1–2 seconds on each rep, then come back.
hatalar: Lifting the heel off the floor.
Letting the knee cave inward to gain the angle that way.
Collapsing the arch and rolling onto the inside of the foot.
ankle.diz: Drive your knee forward in line with your second and third toes; on landings, too, a knee that doesn't cave inward is the alignment you want for your ACL.

ana.detay: the main muscle being stretched because the knee is bent; limits how far the ankle bends forward

yardimci.detay: stretches less because the knee is bent
actively bends the ankle and brings the knee forward

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the knee from caving inward

approach.amac: Turns the speed you build in your approach steps into a vertical jump; directly trains the jump height you need to dunk. A soft two-foot landing teaches you to use that power while protecting the knee.
ipuclari: Build speed over 2–3 steps; make the second-to-last step long and drop low.
Make the last step short and quick, planting both feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing your arms from back to front and up as you extend your ankles, knees and hips together.
At the top, reach with one hand and note the height you touch.
Land softly on both feet, knees bent and in line with your feet; rest 45–60 seconds between reps.
hatalar: Jumping with an upright torso without dropping low in the last steps.
Jumping without swinging the arms.
Landing hard on one foot or with the knees caved in.
approach.diz: The speed of the approach makes the landing harder; land on both feet with knees bent and in line with your feet, and end the set when your jump height drops or your landing breaks down.

ana.detay: explosively opens the hip (extension)
all four heads together; brakes on the last step, then pushes by straightening the knee
gives the final push by extending the ankle (plantar flexion)

yardimci.detay: the long heads help open the hip
front fibers; add to the jump through the arm swing

sabitleyici.detay: stiffens the trunk and helps transfer leg force upward
lumbar portion; keeps the torso upright during the jump
keeps the pelvis level on landing and limits the knee caving inward

askip.amac: Prepares the hip flexors, calves and ankles for jumping. Carries the rhythm of driving the knee up and bringing the foot down under the hip into your running and dunk steps.
ipuclari: Drive your knee up to hip height, thigh parallel to the floor.
Keep the lifted foot's ankle flexed up; don't let your toes droop.
Swing the opposite arm forward and the other back; keep your elbows bent at about 90°.
Strike under your hip with the support foot, short and snappy, on the ball of the foot.
Keep your torso upright; don't lean back.
hatalar: Leaning the torso back to lift the knee.
Letting the ankle go slack and the toes droop.
Bringing the same-side arm and leg forward together.

ana.detay: deep muscle at groin level; pulls the knee up to hip height
push through the ankle of the support foot to create the bounce

yardimci.detay: the quadriceps head that also flexes the hip; joins in the knee drive
flexes the lifted foot's ankle upward
opens the hip as the foot comes down to the floor
help pull the leg down and back

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the pelvis level during single-foot contact
keep the torso upright as the knee rises

bearhug.amac: Teaches you to keep your torso rigid and to breathe under load while walking with a heavy weight hugged to your chest. Directly serves the goal of a torso that takes contact.
ipuclari: Squat down to get the bag into your lap, then pull it to your chest and wrap your arms tightly around it.
Stand tall, pull your shoulders back and keep the bag pinned to your chest.
Walk with short, quick steps.
Keeping your abs braced, take short, controlled breaths.
hatalar: Leaning back and loading the weight onto the lower back.
Letting the bag slide down to the belly and loosening the arms.
Holding your breath for a long time.
bearhug.diz: When picking the bag up off the floor, don't let your knees cave in; if it's very heavy, pick it up from a box.

ana.detay: stiffen the torso through intra-abdominal pressure
keep the spine upright while the load in front pulls the torso forward

yardimci.detay: squeezes the arms around the bag
keep the elbows bent

sabitleyici.detay: limit side bending and rotation of the torso
keeps the pelvis level on every step
upper fibers carry the shoulder girdle under the load

bench.amac: Builds pushing strength in the chest, front delts and triceps. It's the foundation of the upper-body power you need to push opponents away on contact and to set screens.
ipuclari: Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down, and lift your chest slightly.
Press your feet into the floor and keep your hips on the bench.
Lower the bar under control to the middle of your chest, at nipple level.
Keep your elbows at about 45° to your torso.
Press the bar off your chest and slightly back, over your shoulders.
hatalar: Flaring the elbows out to 90°.
Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Lifting the hips off the bench.

ana.detay: mainly the sternocostal head (mid-lower chest); the clavicular head also joins in
extends the elbow; most prominent in the top half of the movement

yardimci.detay: joins the press by raising the arm forward

sabitleyici.detay: hold the shoulder blades steady and control the bar on the way down
keeps the head of the upper-arm bone in its socket

boxjump.amac: Develops vertical explosive power off two feet. Because you land on top of the box, the fall distance is shorter; you train dunking power while putting less landing load on the knee.
ipuclari: Stand in front of a 40–50 cm box, feet hip-width apart.
Swing your arms back and explode onto the box with a quick quarter squat.
Land quietly on the box: hips back, knees in line with your toes.
Stand fully upright on the box, then step down.
End the set if your speed drops or your landings get heavy.
hatalar: Jumping back down off the box.
Picking a box that's too high and landing in a deep squat with the knees at the chest.
The knees caving inward on landing.
boxjump.diz: Jumping down off the box adds a hard drop landing to every rep and increases the load on the knee; always step down from the box.

ana.detay: the vastus muscles straighten the knee explosively and brake the landing
explosively opens the hip

yardimci.detay: push through the ankle for the final acceleration
help open the hip
adds momentum to the jump by swinging the arms forward and up

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the knees aligned on landing
stiffen the torso and transfer power

bridge.amac: Wakes up the glutes before heavy lifts and teaches you to open the hip independently of the lower back. It's the foundation of the hip drive in deadlifts and jumps.
ipuclari: Lie on your back with your feet hip-width apart and your heels close to under your knees.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until they line up with your shoulders and knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and hold for 1 second.
Keep your ribs down; lift your hips, not your lower back.
Keep your knees in line with your feet; don't let them collapse inward.
hatalar: Arching the lower back to gain height.
Not squeezing the glutes and leaving the load to the hamstrings (a cramping feeling in the hamstrings).
Letting the knees drop inward.

ana.detay: lifts the pelvis by opening the hip; contracts hardest at the top

yardimci.detay: help open the hip

sabitleyici.detay: keep the ribs down and prevent arching of the lower back
keeps the knees from collapsing inward

bss.amac: Develops single-leg strength and balance, and exposes differences between your two legs. Strengthens the hip and thigh muscles that support the knee in jumping, landing and changing direction.
ipuclari: Rest the top of your back foot on the bench and set your front foot a comfortable step forward.
Keep the front knee in line with the 2nd and 3rd toes; don't let it cave in.
Lower under control until your back knee nears the floor.
Put the load on the front leg; push through the whole front foot to stand up.
Lean your torso slightly forward to load the glutes; keep it upright to load the quads.
hatalar: The front knee caving inward.
The front foot too close to the bench, with the heel lifting.
Pushing off the back leg and letting the front leg slack off.
bss.diz: The knee drifting inward on one leg is a pattern associated with ACL strain; keeping the front knee in line with the 2nd–3rd toes also builds the right habit for your landings on the court.

ana.detay: on the front leg; the vastus muscles straighten the knee and carry the main load
on the front leg; opens the hip as you rise out of the bottom

yardimci.detay: its rear portion helps open the hip on the front leg
help open the hip and stabilize around the knee

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the pelvis level and limits the front knee caving inward
keep the torso from leaning to the side
grip the dumbbells

cablerow.amac: Strengthens the mid and upper back and the muscles that pull the shoulder blades back. Balances pushing movements like the bench and incline press.
ipuclari: Put your feet on the platform, bend your knees slightly and keep your chest up.
Pull the handle to your belly and squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Drive your elbows back close to your body; don't shrug your shoulders toward your ears.
On the way forward, straighten your arms, let your shoulder blades spread forward, and keep torso sway small.
hatalar: Pulling the weight by throwing the torso back.
Reaching forward by rounding the lower back.
Pulling with the arms only, without moving the shoulder blades at all.

ana.detay: pulls the arm back along the side of the body
draw the shoulder blades together toward the spine
middle fibers pull the shoulder blades back

yardimci.detay: rear fibers pull the arm back
pulls the arm back together with the lats
flex the elbow
joins in elbow flexion with a neutral grip

sabitleyici.detay: keep the torso upright and limit rocking back and forth

calfwall.amac: Relaxes the calf and the area around the Achilles tendon, which take the most load in jumps and landings; maintains the ankle's range for bending forward.
ipuclari: Lean your hands against the wall and extend one foot back.
Keep your back leg straight and your heel on the floor.
Point the toes of your back foot straight ahead.
Push your hips forward and feel the stretch in your calf.
Hold while breathing out; don't bounce.
hatalar: Lifting the back heel off the floor.
Turning the back foot outward.
Forcing it to the point of pain.

ana.detay: the main muscle being stretched because the back knee is straight; medial and lateral heads together

yardimci.detay: partly stretched; becomes the main muscle stretched when the knee bends

contact.amac: Teaches you to stiffen your torso against a push in the air and land balanced on two feet. Prepares you, in a controlled setting, for contact landings under the basket.
ipuclari: Have your partner hold the pad at chest height; keep the pushes light for the first weeks.
Start by knowing which way the push will come; as you get used to it, have your partner vary the direction.
Jump straight up; in the air, brace your abs and back and meet the push with your torso.
Land on both feet, knees bent and in line with your feet; stick the landing.
The push should come while you're in the air, not close to the landing.
hatalar: Leaving the torso loose and getting thrown around by the push.
Landing on one foot or with the knees caved in.
The push being too hard or coming too close to the landing.
contact.diz: Getting pushed in the air and landing off-balance is one of the situations in which ACL injuries occur in basketball; keep the pushes light, land on both feet with bent knees, and stop if your knee feels unstable.

ana.detay: stiffen the torso against the push
keep the torso from rotating and bending sideways when the push comes to the shoulder or at an angle
brakes the knee bending on landing
absorb the landing; keep the pelvis and knee aligned

yardimci.detay: power the jump and take the first contact on landing
contract together with the quadriceps to stabilize the knee

sabitleyici.detay: keep the torso upright against the push

copenhagen.amac: Strengthens the inner-thigh muscles; it's one of the key exercises used to prevent groin injuries. It also works the obliques and hips, and contributes to leg control when changing direction and in contact.
ipuclari: Lie on your side, put your elbow under your shoulder and place your top leg on the bench.
For the first weeks keep your knee on the bench; once you complete the time comfortably, move to the ankle.
Press your top leg into the bench to lift your hips; shoulder, hip and foot in one line.
Lift your bottom leg toward the bench and hold it there for the full time.
Don't hold your breath; don't let your hips drop.
hatalar: The hips sagging or folding backward.
Moving to the long, ankle-supported version before you're ready.
Holding your breath.
copenhagen.diz: In the long, ankle-supported version, the inner side of the top knee takes load; if your knee feels uncomfortable, go back to the short, knee-supported version.

ana.detay: carry the body on the top leg and lift the leg on the bottom leg; adductor longus works noticeably
on the bottom side; keep the torso in a straight side line

yardimci.detay: crosses the hip and knee; assists the inner-thigh muscles
on the bottom side; keeps the pelvis from dropping

sabitleyici.detay: carries body weight on the bottom shoulder
on the bottom arm; holds the shoulder blade against the rib cage

curl.amac: Strengthens the biceps and elbow flexors. Supports arm strength in pulls like rows and pull-ups, and contributes to the upper-body goal.
ipuclari: Stand tall and pin your elbows at your sides.
Start with your palms facing each other and turn your wrists outward as you lift.
Squeeze your biceps for a moment at the top; don't let your elbows drift forward.
Lower the dumbbell over 3 seconds and fully straighten your arm.
hatalar: Swinging the weight up by rocking the torso.
Letting the elbows drift forward and shifting the load to the shoulders.
Lowering fast and not fully straightening the arm at the bottom.

ana.detay: short and long heads flex the elbow; turning the wrist outward (supination) is also its job
beneath the biceps; the main flexor of the elbow

yardimci.detay: helps flex the elbow; its share drops as the palm turns up

sabitleyici.detay: front fibers hold the shoulder in place
keep the wrist straight

dbrow.amac: Strengthens the broad and middle back muscles one side at a time; balances the push of the bench press with a pull. Keeping the torso from rotating also helps you stay solid on contact.
ipuclari: Put your non-working knee and hand on the bench; keep your back flat and nearly parallel to the floor.
Row the dumbbell by driving your elbow toward your hip.
Don't rotate your torso; keep your shoulders parallel to the floor.
At the top, draw your shoulder blade toward your spine, then lower under control.
At the bottom, fully straighten your arm and let your shoulder blade slide slightly forward.
hatalar: Swinging the weight by rotating the torso.
Flaring the elbow out and pulling the dumbbell toward the shoulder.
Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear.

ana.detay: pulls the arm down and back as the elbow travels to the hip
draw the shoulder blade toward the spine

yardimci.detay: pulls the shoulder blade back and down
pulls the arm back
flex the elbow

sabitleyici.detay: keep the torso from rotating
grip the dumbbell

facepull.amac: Strengthens the rear delts, the shoulder-blade muscles and the muscles that rotate the arm outward. Balances pushing movements; it's in the program for the health of your shooting shoulder.
ipuclari: Set the pulley at face height or slightly above, and grab the rope by both ends.
Pull the rope toward your face; keep your elbows high and back.
At the end, bring your hands beside your ears, rotate your arms outward and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Stand tall without leaning back, hold for 1 second and release under control.
hatalar: Using too heavy a load and pulling by throwing the torso back.
Dropping the elbows and turning the movement into a row.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.

ana.detay: rear fibers open the arm out to the side and back
rotate the arm outward; the main target for shoulder health

yardimci.detay: middle and lower fibers pull the shoulder blade back and down
draw the shoulder blades together

sabitleyici.detay: keep the torso from leaning back

farmer.amac: Builds grip strength and shoulder and torso stiffness while walking under heavy load. Trains the whole-body tension you need to stay upright and solid on contact.
ipuclari: Lift the dumbbells off the floor like a deadlift and stand up tall.
Keep your shoulders down and back, away from your ears.
Walk dead straight with short, quick steps.
Brace your abs; don't let your torso lean forward or to the side.
If your grip starts to loosen, stop and set the weights down under control.
hatalar: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
Leaning forward and swaying along with long steps.
Setting the weights down with a rounded back.

ana.detay: grip the handles; usually the first muscles to tire
resists the load pulling the shoulders down

yardimci.detay: opens the hip on every step under load
push off for each step

sabitleyici.detay: keep the torso from leaning to the side
stiffens the torso through intra-abdominal pressure
keeps the pelvis level in each single-leg moment
keep the torso upright

frontsquat.amac: A heavy squat with an upright torso; it feeds the push in your jump by strengthening the quads and glutes. Because the bar is in front, the torso stays upright, and you can get muscle work similar to the back squat with a lighter load.
ipuclari: Set the bar in front of your collarbones, on top of your shoulders; your fingers only balance the bar.
Keep your elbows up and forward; don't let them drop on the way down.
Breathe in, brace your abs and descend with an upright torso; your knees can travel forward toward your toes.
Point your knees the same way as your toes; drive through the whole foot to stand up.
If your wrist mobility isn't enough, cross your arms or use straps.
hatalar: The elbows dropping: the bar slides forward and the torso tips forward.
The heels lifting or the weight shifting onto the toes.
The lower back rounding at the bottom.
frontsquat.diz: The load on the ACL in a squat is low; let your knees travel forward, but don't let them cave in, and stay within a pain-free depth.

ana.detay: vastus lateralis, medialis and intermedius straighten the knee; the upright torso increases the quads' share
opens the hip as you rise from the bottom

yardimci.detay: its rear portion helps open the hip in the deep position

sabitleyici.detay: thoracic portion; keeps the upper back upright and stops the bar from falling forward
lumbar portion; keeps the lower back neutral
stiffens the torso through intra-abdominal pressure
front fibers; hold the arms forward to form the shelf the bar sits on

goblet.amac: The load in front teaches you a deep squat with an upright torso. Lays the foundation of leg and hip strength and prepares you for the front squat that comes after week 3.
ipuclari: Hold the dumbbell vertically, its top end cupped in both palms against your chest.
Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Squat down until your elbows pass between your knees; stop at the deepest pain-free point.
Let your knees travel in the same direction as your toes.
Heels down, chest up; drive through the whole foot to stand up.
hatalar: The heels lifting off the floor.
The knees caving inward.
The lower back rounding and the chest dropping forward at the bottom.
goblet.diz: The load on the ACL in a squat is low; the knee traveling forward is not a problem, the knee caving in and painful depth are.

ana.detay: vastus lateralis, medialis and intermedius straighten the knee; rectus femoris contributes less
opens the hip as you rise from the bottom; its contribution grows with depth

yardimci.detay: its rear portion helps open the hip in the deep position

sabitleyici.detay: keep the torso upright and the spine neutral
stiffens the torso through intra-abdominal pressure
front fibers; hold the dumbbell in front of the chest
carries the load by keeping the elbow bent

hammer.amac: Strengthens the brachialis and brachioradialis, and with them the forearm and grip. A strong grip can contribute to ball control.
ipuclari: Keep your palms facing each other and don't change this grip at any point in the movement.
Keep your elbows fixed at your sides; only your forearms move.
Grip the dumbbell tight and keep your wrist straight, without bending it.
Pause for a moment at the top and lower under control.
hatalar: Swinging the torso to lift.
Turning the wrist in or out while lifting.
Letting the elbow drift forward and bringing the shoulder into it.

ana.detay: in its most effective position for elbow flexion with a neutral grip
the main elbow flexor; not affected by forearm position

yardimci.detay: joins in elbow flexion

sabitleyici.detay: grip the dumbbell tightly
keep the wrist straight at a neutral angle

hamstr.amac: After training, relaxes the hamstrings, which work hard in jumping and sprinting; maintains your range of motion for bending from the hips.
ipuclari: Extend your front leg straight; heel on the floor, toes up.
Bend your back knee slightly and shift your weight onto the back leg.
Keeping your back flat, bend forward from the hips and bring your chest toward your front knee.
Keep your front knee straight, but don't lock it back.
Stop at the point where you feel tension in the back of your thigh, and breathe out.
hatalar: Rounding the back and reaching for the foot with the hands.
Bouncing while stretching.
Forcing it despite burning or tingling behind the knee.

ana.detay: stretch as you bend from the hips with the knee straight

yardimci.detay: with the toes up, tension also builds behind the knee and in the calf
its rear portion works like a hamstring, so it stretches too

sabitleyici.detay: keep the back flat so the bend comes from the hips

hipflexor.amac: Stretches the muscles at the front of the hip after sprinting, jumping and long periods of sitting. Being able to fully open the hip makes room for the hip drive in running and jumping.
ipuclari: Get into a half kneel: back knee on the mat, front knee bent at 90°.
Squeeze the glute on the back-leg side and tuck your pelvis slightly under.
Keeping your torso upright, shift your hips slightly forward.
Reach the arm on the back-leg side overhead and lean slightly to the opposite side.
Feel the stretch at the front of your groin; if you feel it in your lower back, tuck your pelvis a bit more.
hatalar: Arching the lower back and leaning forward.
Just sliding forward without squeezing the glute.
Forcing it to the point of pain.

ana.detay: deep muscle at groin level; the main muscle being stretched on the back leg
stretches on the back leg because the hip is open and the knee is bent

yardimci.detay: stretch along the side of the torso with the arm overhead and the torso leaning to the opposite side

sabitleyici.detay: contracts on the back leg to tilt the pelvis under, increasing the stretch
helps tuck the pelvis under and prevents arching of the lower back

hopstick.amac: Teaches you to absorb force softly when landing on one leg and to keep your knee in line with your foot. It's a core part of the landing control that protects your knee in dunks, rebounds and changes of direction.
ipuclari: Start with a short distance; increase it as you land quietly and balanced.
Touch down on the ball of your foot, bending your hip and knee together as you let the heel down.
On landing, keep your knee in line with the 2nd and 3rd toes; don't let it cave in.
Keep your pelvis level and your torso leaning slightly forward, and hold still for 3 seconds.
If your knee caves in or you lose balance, shorten the distance.
hatalar: Landing hard with the knee nearly straight.
The knee caving inward or the pelvis dropping to one side on landing.
Losing balance for the sake of distance and putting the other foot down.
hopstick.diz: Single-leg landings where the knee caves in and stays nearly straight stress the ACL; landing with the knee bent and in line with your foot reduces that load.

ana.detay: vastus lateralis and medialis; brake the knee bending on landing
absorbs the landing by braking the hip as it bends
keeps the pelvis level; limits the thigh turning inward and the knee caving in

yardimci.detay: push in the hop and take the first contact on landing; soleus also works hard with the knee bent
contract together with the quadriceps on landing, limiting the shin sliding forward

sabitleyici.detay: keep the torso from leaning to the side
outer side of the lower leg; stabilize the ankle against the foot tipping inward

incline.amac: Strengthens the upper chest, front delts and triceps; it's the pushing side of your strong-upper-body goal. Because dumbbells work each arm separately, right–left differences also become visible.
ipuclari: Set the bench to 30°; a steeper angle shifts the load to the front delts.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down, and plant your feet on the floor.
Lower the dumbbells under control to your upper chest; elbows at about 45° to your torso.
As you press up, bring the dumbbells together over your chest.
hatalar: Setting the bench too steep; the movement turns into a shoulder press.
Letting the shoulders roll forward and the shoulder blades spread at the bottom.
Lifting the lower back too far off the bench into a bridge.

ana.detay: the clavicular head (upper chest) works most; the sternocostal portion also joins in

yardimci.detay: front fibers raise the arm forward and up
lateral and medial heads extend the elbow

sabitleyici.detay: stabilize the shoulder by keeping the shoulder blades back and down

kbswing.amac: Teaches you to open the hip explosively (a hinge movement). Because the knee bends only a little, it develops hip power for jumping and the posterior chain without putting much load on the knee.
ipuclari: Grab the kettlebell with both hands slightly in front of your feet and hike it back between your legs.
Bend your knees slightly and push your hips back; the movement is a hinge from the hips, not a squat.
Drive your hips forward explosively; your arms just carry the kettlebell.
At the top, squeeze your glutes and abs and stand tall; don't lean back from the lower back.
As the kettlebell drops, keep your back flat and send your hips back again.
hatalar: Bending the knees too much and turning the movement into a squat.
Lifting the kettlebell with the arms and shoulders.
Leaning back from the lower back at the top or rounding the back at the bottom.

ana.detay: explosively opens the hip; the engine of the movement
the long heads stretch in the hinge and open the hip; the short head of biceps femoris does not cross the hip

yardimci.detay: its rear portion helps open the hip

sabitleyici.detay: lumbar portion; keeps the spine straight throughout the swing
prevents excessive arching of the lower back at the top
keeps the arms close to the body and controls the kettlebell's path
grip the handle

latpull.amac: Builds vertical pulling strength by strengthening the lats and the arm flexors; helps you pull the ball in on rebounds and contributes to a strong upper body. Prepares you for pull-ups.
ipuclari: Lock your knees under the pad and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Lift your chest and lean back slightly.
Start the pull by drawing your shoulder blades down, and pull the bar to your collarbone.
Drive your elbows down and back, beside your ribs.
Let the bar up over 2 seconds and fully straighten your arms at the top.
hatalar: Pulling by swinging the torso and leaning back too far.
Bringing the bar down behind the neck.
Doing half reps without straightening the arms at the top.

ana.detay: lower and outer fibers; draw the arm down and back

yardimci.detay: pulls the arm down together with the latissimus
draw the shoulder blade toward the spine and rotate it downward
lower fibers; pull the shoulder blade down
flex the elbow; the brachialis lies beneath the biceps
rear fibers; help pull the arm back

sabitleyici.detay: stabilizes the torso as you lean back

legswing.amac: Dynamically opens the hip front to back; warms up the hip flexors and hamstrings without load. Prepares the hip's range of motion before sprinting and jumping.
ipuclari: Hold on to the wall with one hand and keep your standing knee slightly bent.
Keep your torso upright; the swing should come from the hip, not the lower back.
Start with a small range and go a little higher with each swing.
Don't fling your leg; swing it rhythmically and under control.
Keep the sole of your standing foot on the floor.
hatalar: Rounding the back and bending forward as the leg comes forward.
Arching the lower back as the leg goes back.
Swinging at full range and speed from the first rep.

ana.detay: swing the leg forward; stretch on the backswing
stretch on the forward swing, pull the leg back

yardimci.detay: swings the leg back
joins the forward swing, stretches on the backswing

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the pelvis balanced on the standing leg
keep the lower back steady during the swing

lunge.amac: Warms up slow lowering control and balance on one leg. Driving the knee to the chest as you rise mimics the takeoff position of a layup and a one-foot dunk.
ipuclari: Step back with one foot and lower your back knee toward the floor over 3 seconds.
Put your weight through the whole front foot; keep your front knee in line with your second and third toes.
Push off the front foot to rise and drive your back knee to your chest.
At the top, balance on one foot for 1 second, keeping your pelvis level.
Bring the opposite arm forward with the knee.
hatalar: Dropping fast and slamming the back knee into the floor.
The front knee caving inward.
Moving to the next rep without holding the balance.
lunge.diz: Stepping back is gentler on the knee because it lacks the sudden braking of a forward lunge; keep your front knee in line with your toes and lower slowly.

ana.detay: on the front leg; brake the descent and lift you by straightening the knee
opens the hip on the front leg

yardimci.detay: drive the back knee to the chest; stretch on the back leg during the descent
helps open the hip at the bottom

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the pelvis level and the knee aligned on one leg
stabilize the ankle during single-leg balance

mbpass.amac: Builds explosive pushing power in the chest, shoulders and arms; teaches you to transfer force that starts in the legs through the torso into the arms. Contributes to hard passes and to the power to push an opponent in contact.
ipuclari: Stand 2–3 m from a wall with one foot forward; hold the ball at your chest with both hands.
Push off the back foot, drive your hips forward and throw the ball explosively into the wall.
Finish the throw with your arms fully extended, thumbs turned down.

conventional_deadlift.diz: The knee bends less and takes less load than with the trap bar; the load sits more on the hips and lower back. Point your knees in line with your feet.

ana.detay: lifts the bar by extending the hip
extend the hip; work harder than with the trap bar

contributes to hip extension

keeps the bar close to the legs
stabilizes the shoulder girdle under load
grip the bar

couch_stretch.amac: With your back foot against the wall, the knee bends fully; by stretching the rectus femoris at both the hip and the knee, it has a stronger effect than the hip flexor stretch.
ipuclari: Put your back knee on the pad at the base of the wall and rest the top of your foot against the wall.
Plant your front foot forward and slowly bring your torso upright.
Squeeze your glutes and tuck your pelvis under.
If it's too intense, put your hands on your front knee and keep your torso leaning forward.
hatalar: Arching the lower back to get upright.
Forcing it to the point of pain.
couch_stretch.diz: Deep knee bending stresses the kneecap more than the ACL; put a thick pad under your knee.

ana.detay: the most stretched muscle, since the hip is extended and the knee fully bent
stretch as the pelvis tilts

yardimci.detay: stretch because the knee is fully bent

sabitleyici.detay: contracts to tilt the pelvis
prevents lower-back arching

dead_bug.amac: Teaches you to keep your lower back steady on the floor while your arms and legs move; it's the foundation for harder core exercises like the Pallof press.
ipuclari: Lie on your back; reach your arms to the ceiling and bend your hips and knees to 90°.
Breathe out, brace your abs and press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg toward the floor.
Return to the start without your lower back lifting, then switch sides.
hatalar: Continuing while the lower back lifts and arches.
Going fast and uncontrolled.
Holding the breath.

ana.detay: hold the lower back on the floor and prevent arching

yardimci.detay: steady the torso during the opposite arm-leg movement
hold the leg in the air; the abs don't let them pull on the lower back

double_leg_calf_raise.amac: Splits the load between both legs and reduces the balance demand. Used as preparation for, or a regression of, the single-leg calf raise.
ipuclari: Stand with the balls of both feet on the edge of the step and hold onto something.
Lower your heels below the step and pause for 1 second.
Rise as high as you can on your toes and hold for 1 second.
When it gets easy, hold a dumbbell or switch to one leg.
hatalar: Bouncing through it quickly.
Shifting the weight to the outer edge of the foot.

ana.detay: medial and lateral heads lift the heel; works most with the knee straight
helps lift the heel; its share grows with the knee bent

yardimci.detay: contributes to lifting the heel

dumbbell_bench_press.amac: Works the same muscles as the bench press; because each arm works on its own, it also improves left–right balance and shoulder control. It gives the shoulder a freer path of movement.
ipuclari: Lie back, bringing the dumbbells from your knees to your chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades and press your feet into the floor.
Lower the dumbbells to mid-chest level, with your elbows at about 45° to your torso.
Bring the dumbbells toward each other as you press up.
hatalar: Flaring the elbows all the way out to the sides.
Lowering the dumbbells so far that the shoulders slide forward.
Dropping the dumbbells to the sides uncontrolled at the end of the set.

ana.detay: mainly the sternocostal head; the clavicular head also contributes
extends the elbow

yardimci.detay: assists the press by raising the arm forward

sabitleyici.detay: keeps each arm stable in its joint independently
hold the shoulder blades steady

dumbbell_deadlift.amac: A light, easy-to-learn version of the trap bar deadlift; it grooves the pattern of pushing your hips back and pushing the floor away with your feet under a light load.
ipuclari: Place the dumbbells beside your feet or just in front of them.
Push your hips back and squat down; grab them with your back flat and chest up.
Push the floor away with your feet and let the dumbbells rise close to your legs.
At the top, squeeze your glutes and stand tall; lower along the same path.
hatalar: Rounding the back to reach for the dumbbells.
Pulling the load with the arms.
Holding the dumbbells away from the legs.
dumbbell_deadlift.diz: Point your knees in the same direction as your toes; make not caving in a habit even with light loads.

ana.detay: lifts by extending the hip
extends the knee

yardimci.detay: assist hip extension

sabitleyici.detay: keep the spine neutral
grip the dumbbells

dynamic_copenhagen_plank.amac: Lowering and raising your hips works the adductors both as they lengthen and as they shorten; it's the bench version of the Copenhagen adduction exercise, which has been researched for preventing groin injuries.
ipuclari: Set up the Copenhagen plank position; work with support at the knee first, then at the ankle.
Lower your hips toward the floor in 2–3 seconds, letting the bottom leg come close to the floor.
Press the top leg into the bench to lift your hips back into line.
On every rep, bring shoulder, hip and foot back into one straight line.
hatalar: Dropping fast and uncontrolled.
Bending at the hips, forward or back.
Moving to the long version too early.
dynamic_copenhagen_plank.diz: In the ankle-supported version, the inner side of the top knee takes load; if your knee feels uncomfortable, work with the knee-supported version.

ana.detay: on the top leg; work lengthening on the way down and shortening on the way up; adductor longus works noticeably
on the bottom side; hold the torso in a straight side line

yardimci.detay: crosses the hip and knee; assists the adductors
on the bottom side; helps lift the hips back up

sabitleyici.detay: carries the body weight on the bottom shoulder

ez_bar_curl.amac: Lets you work the biceps with both arms together, under a heavier load than with dumbbells. The cambered bar holds the wrist at a more comfortable angle than a straight bar.
ipuclari: Grip the bar on the angled sections of the bends, at shoulder width.
Stand tall and pin your elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar to the highest point you can reach without your elbows drifting forward.
Lower in 3 seconds and fully straighten your arms.
hatalar: Swinging the torso to heave the bar up.
Letting the elbows drift forward.

ana.detay: short and long heads flex the elbow
the main elbow flexor

yardimci.detay: contributes to elbow flexion with the semi-supinated grip

sabitleyici.detay: keep the wrist straight

glute_bridge_march.amac: Lifting your feet one at a time while holding the bridge loads the hips one side at a time and trains pelvic stability.
ipuclari: First bridge up on both feet and squeeze your glutes.
Lift one knee toward your chest; don't let your pelvis drop or rotate.
Put your foot back down and switch sides.
Keep your ribs down throughout the movement.
hatalar: The hip dropping to that side when the foot lifts.
Holding the height by arching the lower back.

ana.detay: keeps the hip extended on the support leg

yardimci.detay: assist hip extension on the support leg

sabitleyici.detay: prevents the pelvis from dropping and rotating
stop the torso from rotating

goblet_carry.amac: Walking with the weight held in front of your chest is a lighter, easier-to-grip version of the sandbag carry. It teaches you to stay upright against a load coming from the front.
ipuclari: Hold the dumbbell upright by one end with both hands in front of your chest.
Keep your elbows down and close to your body.
Stand tall, bring your shoulders back and walk with short steps.
Keep your abs braced and breathe under control.
hatalar: Leaning back.
Letting the weight drift away from the chest and tiring out the arms.

ana.detay: stiffen the torso with intra-abdominal pressure
keep the torso upright

yardimci.detay: hold the weight in front of the chest
front fibers keep the weight from dropping

sabitleyici.detay: limit rotation and side bending of the torso
keeps the pelvis level with every step

half_kneeling_ankle_rock.amac: Trains ankle dorsiflexion without needing a wall. If you like, you can place a light weight on your knee to increase the angle.
ipuclari: Get into a half-kneeling position with your front foot flat on the floor.
Without lifting your heel, rock your knee forward past your toes.
Move your knee in line with your second and third toes.
Pause for 1–2 seconds at the end, then come back.
hatalar: Lifting the heel off the floor.
Letting the knee drift inward.
half_kneeling_ankle_rock.diz: Drive your knee forward in line with your toes; letting it drift in makes the angle look bigger than it is and rehearses the alignment you don't want on landings.

ana.detay: the main muscle stretched, since the knee is bent

yardimci.detay: dorsiflexes the ankle and moves the knee forward

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the knee from drifting inward

half_kneeling_landmine_press.amac: Because the bar rises along an angled path, it's a press that can feel easier on the shoulder; the half-kneeling stance also trains torso and hip stability.
ipuclari: Half-kneel facing the bar, with the knee on your pressing-arm side on the floor.
Hold the end of the bar in front of your shoulder; brace your abs and squeeze the glute of the leg on the floor.
Press the bar up and forward, fully straighten your arm and let your shoulder blade glide forward.
Don't rotate your torso or arch your lower back.
hatalar: Leaning back from the lower back.
Pressing by rotating the torso.
Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear.

ana.detay: front fibers; raises the arm forward and up
clavicular head (upper chest); contributes to the angled press
extends the elbow

upper and lower fibers; rotate the shoulder blade up

sabitleyici.detay: prevent torso rotation when pressing with one arm
prevents lower-back arching
keeps the hip extended on the leg on the floor

high_knees.amac: Like the A-skip, it warms up the hip flexors and calves; its faster rhythm also raises your heart rate.
ipuclari: Run in place at a fast tempo, pulling your knees up to hip height.
Land with your foot under your hip, on the ball of the foot.
Keep your torso upright and your arms working opposite your legs.
Start slow and pick up the tempo over a few seconds.
hatalar: Leaning back to lift the knees.
Landing hard on the heels.

ana.detay: drive the knee up fast
push off the floor with each step

yardimci.detay: contributes to hip flexion
brings the leg down to the floor

sabitleyici.detay: keep the torso upright

incline_dumbbell_curl.amac: Because the arm stays behind the body, it works the long head of the biceps in a stretched position. It's harder than a regular curl with the same weight.
ipuclari: Set the bench to 45–60°, lean back and let your arms hang straight down.
Keep your elbows fixed back; don't bring them forward.
Turn your wrist outward as you lift and squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower in 3 seconds and fully straighten your arm.
hatalar: Lifting the shoulders off the bench and sliding forward.
Using your regular curl weight; this variation needs lighter dumbbells.

ana.detay: long head works in a stretched position because the shoulder is back
the main elbow flexor

yardimci.detay: assists elbow flexion

incline_dumbbell_y_raise.amac: Raising your arms in a Y shape while lying face down on an incline bench works the lower traps and rear delts. It improves shoulder blade control with the arm overhead; it carries over to overhead movements like shooting.
ipuclari: Set the bench to 30–45° and lie face down with your chest on the pad.
Hold the dumbbells with your thumbs pointing up.
Raise your arms forward and up so they form a Y with your body.
Hold for 1 second at the top, then lower slowly without shrugging your shoulders to your ears.
hatalar: Choosing heavy dumbbells and shrugging them up.
Lifting the chest off the pad and using the lower back.

ana.detay: lower fibers pull the shoulder blade down and rotate it up
rear and middle fibers raise the arm

yardimci.detay: keep the arm externally rotated

jump_and_reach.amac: Trains the approach jump when you don't have a hoop; the mark on the wall lets you measure your touch height and track your progress.
ipuclari: Approach parallel to the wall; take 2–3 steps and drop low on the second-to-last step.
Jump off both feet and reach as high as you can with the arm nearer the wall.
Put chalk on your fingertips or mark with tape; measure your highest mark.
Land softly on both feet, leaving enough distance so you don't hit the wall.
hatalar: Jumping too close to the wall and hitting it with the shoulder.
Bending the torso sideways while reaching and landing off balance.
Landing on one foot or landing hard.
jump_and_reach.diz: As in the approach jump, land on both feet with your knees bent and in line with your feet; end the set when your jump drops off.

ana.detay: extends the hip explosively
brakes on the last step, then pushes by extending the knee
gives the final push by extending the ankle

yardimci.detay: long heads assist hip extension
front fibers; swing the arm and reach it up

sabitleyici.detay: stiffens the torso and helps transfer force
limit side bending of the torso when reaching with one arm

jump_squat.amac: Stands in for the box jump when you don't have a box: it produces maximal vertical power off both feet. Since you land from higher than with a box, you need to land softly and stabilize on every rep.
ipuclari: Feet hip-width apart; swing your arms back and drop into a fast quarter squat.
Swing your arms up and explode as high as you can.
Land quietly, from the balls of your feet to the whole foot, with your hips back.
Find your balance and stop on every rep; don't bounce the reps back to back.
End the set when your speed drops.
hatalar: Landing hard on straight knees.
The knees caving in on landing.
Bouncing the reps without stopping.
jump_squat.diz: Unlike the box jump, you land from full height; meet the ground with your knees bent and in line with your toes, and end the set if your landings get hard.

ana.detay: extends the knee explosively; brakes the load on landing
extends the hip explosively; takes the landing with the hips

assist hip extension; stabilize the knee on landing
adds momentum to the jump through the arm swing

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the knee from caving in on landing
keep the torso steady on landing

kettlebell_deadlift.amac: Teaches the hip hinge, the foundation of the swing, slowly and under control; strengthens the glutes and hamstrings.

Push your hips back and bend your knees slightly; back flat, chest facing forward.
Grip the handle with both hands and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Push the floor away with your feet and stand tall by bringing your hips forward; squeeze your glutes at the top.

Leaning back from the lower back at the top.

long heads stretch in the hinge and extend the hip

extends the knee at the start of the lift

keeps the kettlebell close to the body
grip the handle

kneeling_medicine_ball_chest_pass.amac: Takes the leg drive out of the movement to focus on explosive pushing from the upper body and torso; an easy starting point for learning the technique.

Push the ball explosively into the wall and fully straighten your arms.
Keep your torso steady without leaning back; make every rep maximum speed.

Throwing by leaning back from the lower back.
Pushing the ball slowly instead of throwing it fast.

extends the elbow fast
front fibers; raise the arm forward

yardimci.detay: pushes the shoulder blade forward to lengthen the throw

sabitleyici.detay: stabilizes the torso without support from the legs
keeps the hip extended

kneeling_medicine_ball_slam.amac: Takes the legs out of the movement to focus the slam on the abs and back muscles. Good for learning the slam or doing a lighter version of it.

Lift the ball overhead and brace your abs.
Bend your torso forward and slam the ball into the floor in front of your knees with all your strength.

long head joins in pulling the arm down at the shoulder

landmine_180.amac: With your arms extended, you move the end of the bar from beside one hip to beside the other. It takes you from resisting rotation, as in the Pallof press, to controlling rotation; it serves torso control in contact and when passing.

Lower the bar in an arc to beside one hip, then carry it to the other side.
Let your hips and torso turn together; your back heel can pivot in the direction of the turn.
Don't bend your arms; steer the movement with your torso.

Keeping the hips still and twisting only from the lower back.
Twisting the knees while the feet are planted.

yardimci.detay: rotate the hip and steer the pelvis
keeps the arms extended

sabitleyici.detay: stiffen the torso
stabilize the spine against the rotational load

landmine_squat.amac: Holding the end of the bar at your chest makes you squat with an upright torso; similar to the goblet squat but allows heavier loading. Because the bar travels in an arc, balance is easy to find.

Lean slightly into the bar, elbows pointing down.
With your knees tracking toward your toes, descend with an upright torso to a pain-free depth.
Push through your whole foot to stand up; squeeze your glutes at the top.

The knees caving in.
The lower back rounding at the bottom.
landmine_squat.diz: The load on the ACL in a squat is low; keep your knee in line with your foot and stay at a pain-free depth.

extends the hip coming up out of the bottom

yardimci.detay: posterior portion assists hip extension in the deep position

sabitleyici.detay: stiffens the torso
keep the torso upright
front fibers; hold the end of the bar in front of the chest

lateral_hop_and_stick.amac: Teaches you to control the hip and knee on a single-leg landing to the side; prepares you for defensive slides and changes of direction.

Touch down on the front of your foot and land softly by bending at the hip and knee.
Keep your knee over your toes; don't let it drift in.
Keep your torso upright and your pelvis level, and hold still for 3 seconds.
If your knee caves in, shorten the distance.
hatalar: The torso swaying to the side on landing.
The knee caving in.
The ankle rolling outward.
lateral_hop_and_stick.diz: On landings to the side it's harder to keep the knee in line with the foot; start with a short distance and don't let your knee drift in.

keep the torso from tipping sideways

lateral_leg_swing.amac: Opens the hip side to side; warms up the inner thigh and outer hip muscles. Good preparation before lateral slides and sudden changes of direction.
ipuclari: Face the wall and hold on with both hands.
Swing one leg across the front of your body and then out to the side.
Keep your pelvis and torso still; let the movement come from the hip.
Start with a small range and widen it gradually.
hatalar: Tilting the torso sideways along with the leg.
Increasing the range by rotating the pelvis.

move the leg out to the side; stretch on the inward swing

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the pelvis level on the support leg
keep the torso from tipping sideways

lateral_lunge.amac: Warms up the hip side to side: it stretches the adductors on one leg while preparing the other leg for the lateral slide and change-of-direction position.
ipuclari: Take a wide step out to the side, with the toes of both feet pointing forward.
Push your hips back and sit onto the leg you stepped with; keep the other leg straight.
Keep the working knee in line with your toes and your heel on the floor.
Keep your chest up and push off the working foot to return to the middle.
hatalar: Letting the working knee go inward and far past the toes.
Rounding the back and leaning forward.
Lifting the heel of the working foot.
lateral_lunge.diz: In a side step, the knee caving in is an unwanted alignment for the ACL; if your knee isn't pointing the same way as your foot, reduce the depth.

brakes the descent and extends the knee on the working leg

yardimci.detay: stretch on the straight leg; control the descent on the working leg

sabitleyici.detay: keeps the knee in line with the foot
keep the back flat

leg_extension.amac: Strengthens the quads in isolation. For someone with an ACL history it's done through a limited range, from 90° to 45° of knee bend; in this range the strain on the ACL is low.

Start with your knee bent at 90° and stop at about 45°.

Keep your hips in the seat and grip the handles.
hatalar: Extending the knee until it's fully straight.
Swinging the weight up.
Lifting the hips off the seat.
leg_extension.diz: In the last 30–45° of knee extension, the quadriceps pull the shin forward and strain the ACL; that's why you keep the movement in the 90°→45° range.

lying_hamstring_stretch.amac: With your back supported on the floor, it stretches the hamstrings without your lower back rounding; a good option when you don't want to deal with balancing on your feet.
ipuclari: Lie on your back with one leg straight on the floor.
Raise the other leg; hold it behind the thigh or with a towel looped around your foot.
Keeping your knee as straight as you can, pull your leg toward you.
Don't let the leg on the floor or your hips lift off the floor.
hatalar: Bending the knee of the leg on the floor or lifting the hips.
Bouncing by yanking the leg.

ana.detay: stretch as the hip flexes and the knee straightens

yardimci.detay: also stretches if you pull your foot toward you

machine_calf_raise.amac: Lets you load the calves heavily without needing balance. It's the machine counterpart of the single-leg calf raise.
ipuclari: Place the balls of your feet on the edge of the platform with your heels hanging free.
Keep your knees straight but not locked.
Lower your heels and pause for 1 second; rise onto your toes and hold for 1 second.
If you're using the leg press, make sure your feet don't slip off the platform.
hatalar: Lifting very heavy weight with half reps.
Bending the knees and doing the movement with the legs.

ana.detay: medial and lateral heads lift the heel; works most with the knee straight
helps lift the heel; its share grows with the knee bent

yardimci.detay: contributes to lifting the heel

machine_incline_chest_press.amac: Works the muscles of the incline dumbbell press without needing balance, thanks to the machine's fixed path. Useful when you have no dumbbells or want to add load safely.
ipuclari: Set the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down and rest your back on the pad.
Press the handles up and forward; don't lift your shoulders off the pad.
Return under control in 2 seconds; don't let the plates clang together.
hatalar: Working without adjusting the seat and pressing the handles from the wrong height.
Rolling the shoulders forward and lifting the shoulder blades off the pad.

ana.detay: works mainly through the clavicular head (upper chest)

yardimci.detay: front fibers raise the arm forward and up
lateral and medial heads extend the elbow

machine_seated_row.amac: Because the chest pad holds the torso steady, the load goes straight to the mid-back. It works the muscles of the cable row independently of the lower back.
ipuclari: Set the seat so the handles sit slightly below your shoulders.
Rest your chest on the pad and keep it there throughout.
Pull the handles by driving your elbows back, and squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
As you extend your arms, let your shoulder blades spread forward.
hatalar: Lifting the chest off the pad and pulling with the torso.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.

pull the shoulder blades together
middle fibers pull the shoulder blades back

yardimci.detay: rear fibers pull the arm back
flex the elbow

medicine_ball_jump_catch.amac: With no partner, it trains you to stiffen your torso against the jolt of a ball caught in the air and to land balanced; similar to grabbing a rebound in the air and landing.

Jump, catch the ball with both hands at the highest point and pull it to your chest.
Brace your abs as you catch; land on both feet, knees bent and in line with your feet.
Hold your balance for 2 seconds on landing, then repeat.
hatalar: Chasing the ball and landing while drifting forward or sideways.
Landing on one foot or with straight knees.
Choosing a ball that's too heavy.
medicine_ball_jump_catch.diz: Landing off balance while chasing the ball stresses the knee; toss the ball close enough that you can control it and stick every landing on both feet.

ana.detay: stiffens the torso during the catch
brakes knee bending on landing
absorb the landing; keep the pelvis and knee aligned

yardimci.detay: drives the jump and takes the first contact on landing
front fibers; reach the arms up and catch the ball

sabitleyici.detay: prevent torso rotation when the ball drifts to the side
keep the torso upright

medicine_ball_scoop_toss.amac: Throwing the ball into the wall while turning sideways teaches you to produce explosive power through hip and torso rotation. It replaces the slam; it serves torso power in contact and when passing.

Squat slightly and shift your weight onto your back leg.
Explosively rotate your back hip forward and scoop the ball from low to high into the wall.
Keep your arms straight and relaxed; let the power come from your hips and torso.
Do every rep at maximum speed and work both sides equally.
hatalar: Throwing the ball with the arms alone.
Keeping the hips still and turning only from the lower back.
medicine_ball_scoop_toss.diz: As you rotate, pivot your back heel too; don't turn your knee inward independently of your foot.

ana.detay: rotate the torso; the external oblique on one side and the internal oblique on the opposite side work together
explosively extends and rotates the hip on the back leg

yardimci.detay: stabilizes the torso and transfers force to the arms
front fibers direct the ball upward

sabitleyici.detay: keep the spine upright during the rotation
keeps the pelvis and knee in line

neutral_grip_lat_pulldown.amac: A vertical pull with your palms facing each other; it can feel easier on the shoulder. It works the same back muscles as the lat pulldown and brings in more of the brachioradialis among the elbow flexors.
ipuclari: Grab the parallel handle and lock your knees under the pad.
Lift your chest, lean back slightly, and pull the handle to your upper chest.
Drive your elbows down to the sides of your ribs.
Let it back up over 2 seconds and fully straighten your arms at the top.
hatalar: Swinging your torso to pull.
Shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears.
Doing half reps.

ana.detay: draws the arm down and back; with the elbows close to the body, it does more of the backward pull

pull the shoulder blade toward the spine
flex the elbow

partner_medicine_ball_chest_pass.amac: Trains the same explosive push by throwing to a partner instead of a wall; catching the incoming ball also teaches you to brake the load and push it right back.

Push off your back foot and throw the ball from chest height to your partner's chest.
Finish with your arms fully extended, thumbs turned down.
Catch the incoming ball softly, close to your chest, and throw it again right away.
hatalar: Throwing with your arms only.

Lower back rounding at the bottom → Limit the depth
Not knowing the locking mechanism → Test the hooks and stops before you start

ipuclari: Lean your back against the wall, walk your feet forward and slide down the wall.
Bend your knees only to a pain-free angle; 90° is the hardest angle and puts the most pressure on the knee.
Knees over your ankles, in line with your feet.
Don't hold your breath; start at 20 s and build up.
hatalar: Knees travelling far past the toes → Move your feet a little further from the wall
Holding your breath → Breathe steadily
Holding at a painful angle → Hold at a shallower angle

ipuclari: Feet wider than shoulders, toes turned out 30–45°.
Let the dumbbell or kettlebell hang between your legs with both hands.
Let your knees open out in line with your toes; torso upright.
Increase depth slowly without forcing the stretch in your groin.
hatalar: Knees drifting inside the feet → Push your knees out in line with your feet
Stance too wide → Stand at a pain-free width
Leaning forward and rounding the lower back → Keep your chest up

ipuclari: Take a long step forward, land heel first and bend both knees.
Front knee in line with your foot; let your back knee come close to the floor.
Push hard off your front foot to come back.
Braking the landing loads the knee; if your knee is sensitive, do reverse lunges first.
hatalar: Dropping down as if falling forward → Keep your torso upright and lower under control
Front knee caving inward → Keep your knee over the middle of your foot
Heel lifting → Keep your whole foot on the floor

ipuclari: Lunge forward, bring your back foot through and move into the next step.
On every step, front knee in line with your foot and torso upright.
Dumbbells at your sides; if your balance goes, reduce the weight.
As you tire, your step shortens and your knee slides forward; stop when quality drops.
hatalar: Steps getting shorter with fatigue → Shorten the distance and keep your stride length
Knees caving inward → Keep your knee in line with your foot
Banging the back knee on the floor → Lower under control

ipuclari: Place your whole foot on the step; push through that foot to step up.
Don't bounce off the bottom foot; let the top leg carry the load.
Keep your knee in line with your foot; lower down slowly.
Choose the step height based on knee pain and your level; a low step suits rehabilitation.
hatalar: Jumping off the bottom foot → Lift the bottom heel slightly and step up using only the top leg
Knee caving inward → Squeeze your outer hip
Step too high → Choose a height where your knee doesn't rise above hip level

ipuclari: Stand on one foot in front of a box, the other foot held in the air in front.
Send your hips back, sit onto the box under control and stand up on one leg.
The lower the box, the harder it is; it's a stepping stone to the pistol.
Keep your knee in line with your foot; compare reps between your two legs.
hatalar: Knee caving inward → Raise the box and strengthen your outer hip
Dropping onto the box → Take 2–3 seconds to lower
Rocking for momentum to stand up → Reach your arms forward and stand up with balance

ipuclari: Stand on one foot and extend the other leg forward; arms forward.
Go to full depth with your heel staying down; don't let the front leg touch the floor.
Keep lower-back rounding at the bottom limited and stand up on one leg.
Start by working with a box or holding on to a post.
hatalar: Heel lifting → Work on ankle mobility or put a plate under your heel
Knee caving inward → Go back to a higher box
Losing control at the bottom and falling → Work with something to hold on to

ipuclari: From a very wide stance, squat down onto one leg; the other leg stays straight with the toes pointing up.
Heel of the squatting side stays down, knee in line with your foot.
Arms forward or a weight at your chest makes balance easier.
Increase the depth only as far as your groin allows.
hatalar: Heel lifting → Reduce the depth
Forcing the groin → Stay at a pain-free angle
Lower back rounding → Keep your chest up and use something to hold on to

ipuclari: Stand on one foot; bend the other leg behind you and hold the foot with the same-side hand.
Lower until your back knee gently touches the floor, then stand up on one leg.
Your torso leans forward; front knee in line with your foot.
Start with partial depth and a cushion under your back knee.
hatalar: Banging the back knee on the floor → Use a cushion and lower under control
Front knee caving inward → Go back to partial depth
Heel lifting → Keep your weight over your midfoot

ipuclari: Rest your shoulder blades on the edge of the bench; place the bar in your hip crease with a pad.
Feet flat on the floor, at a distance where your knees are at 90° at the top.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips into a straight line with your torso; chin slightly tucked.
Squeeze your glutes at the top; don't arch your lower back.
hatalar: Arching the lower back at the top → Keep your ribs down and tilt your pelvis back
Bar pressing on the bone → Use a thick pad
Feet too far away → Bring your feet closer

ipuclari: Hold the bar standing; keep your knees slightly bent and fixed.
Lean forward by pushing your hips back; let the bar slide close to your legs.
Go down as far as your back stays neutral and you feel tension in your hamstrings (usually just below the knee).
Stand up by driving your hips forward; don't lean back at the top.
hatalar: Lower back rounding → Shorten the range and reduce the load
Bar drifting away from the legs → Lower the bar brushing your legs
Bending the knees a lot like a squat → Keep your knees fixed and send your hips back

ipuclari: Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs; knees slightly bent.
Hinge by pushing your hips back; let the dumbbells travel down close to your legs.
Stop where you feel tension in your hamstrings while your back is still neutral.
Stand up by squeezing your glutes.
hatalar: Lower back rounding → Shorten the range
Dumbbells hanging forward → Keep the dumbbells close to your legs
Shoulders rolling forward → Keep your shoulder blades slightly back and down

ipuclari: One foot flat in front; only the toes of the back foot touch the floor, like a kickstand.
Most of the load is on the front leg; hinge by pushing your hips back.
Pelvis level, back neutral.
It's a stepping stone to the single-leg RDL without the full balance challenge.
hatalar: Loading the back foot → Use the back foot only for balance
Pelvis opening up → Keep both hip bones facing the floor
Lower back rounding → Shorten the range

ipuclari: Stand on one foot, knee slightly bent.
As your torso leans forward, let the free leg reach back; head, hip and heel in one line.
Keep your pelvis parallel to the floor; don't let it open up.
Holding the weight in the hand opposite the standing leg works the outer hip more.
hatalar: Pelvis rotating open to the side → Keep the toes of your back foot pointing at the floor
Lower back rounding → Shorten the range
Locking the standing knee → Keep the knee slightly bent

ipuclari: Bar on your back as in a back squat; knees slightly bent.
Lean forward by pushing your hips back, back neutral.
Stop before your torso reaches parallel to the floor, before your back loses its neutral position.
Start light; because the load is far from the spine, the leverage is large.
hatalar: Lower back rounding → Shorten the range and cut the load a lot
Loading heavy → Stay well below your RDL weight
Bending the knees too much → Keep your knees fixed

ipuclari: Lie on your back with your heels on top of the ball.
Lift your hips as in a bridge, then roll the ball in by pulling your heels towards your hips.
Keep your hips up; go slowly as you straighten back out.
Once it gets easier, do it on one leg.
hatalar: Hips dropping → Keep your hips up on every rep
Arching the lower back → Brace your abs
Ball rolling off to the side → Spread your arms out on the floor

ipuclari: Lie face down; knee aligned with the machine's axis, pad just above your Achilles tendon.
Keeping your hips on the pad, pull your heels towards your hips.
Lower slowly; don't fully lock your leg at the bottom.
If there's a strength difference between your legs, also train one leg at a time.
hatalar: Hips lifting off the pad → Press your hips into the pad and reduce the load
Lowering fast → Take 3 s to lower
Continuing through a cramp → Stop, stretch and reduce the load

ipuclari: Knee axis aligned with the machine; let the thigh pad lock your legs in place.
Because the hip is bent, the hamstrings work in a more lengthened position.
Pull your heels down and back, then let them return slowly.
Leaning your torso slightly forward increases the lengthening effect.
hatalar: Loose thigh pad → Set the pad snug
Swinging to pull → Reduce the load and pull under control
One leg doing most of the work → Add single-leg sets

ipuclari: Back upright, pads on the outside of your knees.
Open your legs under control, hold for 1 s, close slowly.
Leaning your torso slightly forward works the upper part of the glutes more.
Strengthening the hip muscles is recommended for knee pain.
hatalar: Bouncing the weight → Reduce the load
Swinging with your torso → Lean your back against the pad
Partial range → Work through a full, pain-free range

ipuclari: Pads on the inside of your knees; start at a width that doesn't strain your groin.
Close your legs under control, open them slowly.
If your groin is sensitive, narrow the starting width.
Inner-thigh strength is linked with groin injury risk; training it regularly may be protective.
hatalar: Starting too wide → Keep the opening at a pain-free limit
Bouncing the weight → Work under control
Continuing despite groin pain → Stop and reduce the load

ipuclari: Lie on your side, bottom knee slightly bent, top leg straight.
Lift the top leg slightly behind you, with your toes pointing forward.
Don't let your pelvis roll back; lower slowly.
Once it gets easier, add a band or ankle weight.
hatalar: Turning the toes towards the ceiling → Keep your toes pointing forward
Pelvis rolling back → Try it with your back against a wall
Bringing the leg forward → Keep the leg in line with your torso or slightly behind

ipuclari: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent about 45°, heels together.
Lift the top knee without separating your heels; keep your pelvis still.
Lower slowly; once it gets easier, add a band above your knees.
It's a very low-load exercise suited to the first days of rehabilitation.
hatalar: Pelvis rolling back → Keep your top hip tilted forward
Doing it fast → Lift for 2 s, lower for 2 s
Heels separating → Press your heels together

ipuclari: Put the band above your knees or around your ankles; get into a half-squat position.
Take small steps sideways or diagonally; keep the band taut.
Don't let your knees cave in; keep your torso upright.
With the band at your ankles, it gets harder.
hatalar: Knees caving inward → Push your knees out
Swinging your torso to step → Keep your torso still and take smaller steps
Band going slack → Don't bring your feet together

ipuclari: Balls of your feet on the edge of the step, heels hanging free.
Knees straight; rise as high as you can onto your toes and hold for 1 s.
Lower your heels slowly below the level of the step.
Keep the full range of motion even on high-rep sets.
hatalar: Going fast like bouncing → 2 s up, 2–3 s down
Partial range → Go all the way up and down
Ankle rolling outward → Keep the weight over your big toe and second toe

ipuclari: With the knee bent at 90°, the soleus works more.
Pad or dumbbell on top of your knees; balls of your feet on the step.
Rise all the way up, then lower slowly.
If your Achilles tendon is sensitive, it's a good first loading step.
hatalar: Partial range → Full range
Bouncing → Controlled tempo
Pad pressing on the kneecap → Place the pad on your thighs

ipuclari: Lean your back against a wall, heels one step out from the wall.
Keeping your heels down, lift the fronts of your feet as high as you can.
Lower slowly; don't let your feet slap the floor.
Moving your heels further from the wall makes it harder.
hatalar: Hips coming off the wall → Keep your back on the wall
Doing it fast → Controlled tempo
Continuing despite pain at the front of the shin → Stop and reduce the load

ipuclari: Stand an arm's length from the wall, hands at shoulder height and shoulder-width apart.
Keep your body in a straight line from heels to head; bring your chest towards the wall and push back.
The further your feet are from the wall, the harder it gets; once it's easy, step back.
Adding a 'plus' at the end by pushing your shoulder blades forward works the serratus.
hatalar: Leaving the hips behind and only reaching your head to the wall → Brace your abs and move your body as one piece
Flaring the elbows out at shoulder height → Keep your elbows at 30–45° to your torso

ipuclari: Place your hands shoulder-width apart on a sturdy surface (table, counter, bench).
The lower the surface, the higher the load: ~41% of body weight at 61 cm, ~55% at 30 cm.
Lower until your chest touches the edge; keep your elbows at 30–45° to your torso.
Hips and shoulders rise together; don't let your lower back sag.
hatalar: Lower back sagging → Squeeze your glutes and abs and hold the plank position
Using a surface that slides → Choose a stable, non-slip surface

ipuclari: Put something soft under your knees; body straight from knees to head.
The load is about 49% of body weight; a regular push-up is 64%.
Lower until your chest is close to the floor; elbows at 30–45°.
If your wrists hurt, use fists or push-up handles.
hatalar: Hips left behind in a broken line → Bring your hips forward and form a straight line from knees to shoulders
Half reps → Lower until your chest is a fist's height from the floor

ipuclari: Place your hands about 1.5 times shoulder width apart; any wider strains the shoulder.
Lower until your chest is level with your hands; don't push your shoulders forward at the bottom.
A wide hand position lowers chest and triceps activity compared with a narrow one; use it if you want chest-focused variety.
hatalar: Lowering the chest far below the hands → Stop when your chest reaches hand level
Hands too wide → Don't go beyond 1.5 times shoulder width

ipuclari: In a wide push-up position, work only the top half: lower until your elbows reach ~90°.
The short range reduces the end-range load of the wide push-up; it works as an intermediate step when your shoulder is sensitive.
Lower to the same depth on every rep; increase the range over time.
On high-rep sets (e.g. 3×20), don't let your form break down on the last reps.
hatalar: Depth getting shallower from rep to rep → Put a cushion under your chest and lower towards it
Raising the hips → Keep your body straight

ipuclari: Bring your index fingers and thumbs together under your chest to form a diamond.
Lower with your elbows close to your torso; let your chest touch your hands.
A narrow hand position increases chest and triceps activity compared with a wide one.
If your wrists strain, move your hands slightly apart (close-grip push-up) — most of the effect is kept.
hatalar: Flaring the elbows out → Let your elbows brush your ribs
Continuing despite wrist pain → Widen your hands slightly or use handles

ipuclari: Put your feet on a surface 30–60 cm high; the load rises to ~70–74% of body weight.
The higher you go, the more the front delts work; a very steep angle gets close to a pike push-up.
Squeeze your abs and glutes so your lower back doesn't sag.
Keep your head neutral; bring your chest, not your forehead, towards the floor.
hatalar: Lower back arching → Squeeze your glutes and bring your ribs down
Leading with the head and hitting the floor → Lower with your chest, chin slightly tucked

ipuclari: Place your hands very wide; bend one arm and lower towards that side while the other arm stays straight as support.
The straight arm only supports; most of the load is on the bending arm.
Don't let your torso rotate; keep your hips parallel to the floor.
It's an intermediate step to the one-arm push-up; train both sides equally.
hatalar: Torso rotating towards the bending arm → Brace your abs and keep your hips level
Loading the straight-arm shoulder at an extreme angle → Keep the straight arm slightly below shoulder level

ipuclari: Feet wider than your shoulders; working hand under your chest, the other hand behind your back.
Your torso may rotate slightly, but don't let your hips drop.
Start with one-arm push-ups on an incline and gradually lower the surface.
Low reps, long rest: it's a skill and strength move.
hatalar: Hips sagging and torso twisting → Widen your feet and brace your abs and obliques
Trying too early and forcing reps → Meet the archer push-up benchmark and start on an incline

ipuclari: Set the seat so the handles are level with the middle of your chest.
In the starting position, keep the handles in front of your body; don't let your shoulders open back too far.
Push under control, return under control; don't let the weights crash onto the stack.
A good starting exercise for beginners and people with sensitive shoulders.
hatalar: Seat set too low → Set it so the handles are at mid-chest
Starting with the arms far behind the body → Use the range-of-motion limiter

ipuclari: Lock your elbows in a slight bend; move only at the shoulder.
Open the dumbbells down to chest level, no lower.
Choose a light-to-moderate weight; torque is large with long arms.
Bring your arms together at the top and squeeze your chest.
hatalar: Opening the arms far below the body → Stop with your elbows level with your torso
Straightening the elbows → Lock your elbows at a 15–30° bend
Turning it into a press with heavy weight → Reduce the load and lower slowly

ipuclari: On the pec deck, set the seat so the handles are slightly below shoulder level.
Don't let your arms open back past the line of your torso.
With cables, resistance is more even through the movement; you can change the angles (high, low).
Light-to-moderate load, 10–20 reps.
hatalar: Opening the arms too far back on the pec deck → Set the range limiter
Rounding the shoulders forward → Keep your chest open and shoulder blades back

ipuclari: Place your hands behind you on a stable surface and grip the edge with your fingers pointing forward.
Lower until your elbows reach 90°; don't go lower.
Start with your knees bent; straightening or raising your feet makes it harder.
Keep your back close to the bench; shoulders away from your ears.
hatalar: Going so deep the elbows pass 90° → Stop with your elbows at 90°
Rounding the shoulders forward and shrugging them to the ears → Keep your chest open and shoulders down
Hips drifting away from the bench → Slide your back closer to the bench

ipuclari: First learn to hold a 30 s support on top of the bars with arms straight and shoulders down.
Lower until your elbows reach ~90°; stop when your shoulders drop slightly below your elbows.
Leaning your torso slightly forward emphasises the chest; staying upright emphasises the triceps.
First step: slow lowering only (negative dips), then full reps.
Ring dips demand far more shoulder control; they come after bar dips.
hatalar: Going too deep → Stop with your elbows at 90°
Shoulders shrugging up to the ears → Press your shoulder blades down
Swinging to get reps → Keep your legs still and lower slowly

ipuclari: Standing, bar resting over your collarbones; grip slightly wider than your shoulders, wrists straight.
Squeeze your glutes and abs; press the bar straight up past your face and move your head forward once the bar passes.
At the top, arms in line with your ears, shoulders slightly shrugged.
Always press in front; behind-the-neck pressing forces the shoulder into a 'high-five' position.
hatalar: Arching the lower back to press → Squeeze your glutes and abs and reduce the load
Behind-the-neck press → Lower and press the bar in front
Pressing the bar far from the face → Keep the bar close to your face in a vertical line

ipuclari: Start with your palms facing you; turn them forward as you press.
Make the rotation slow and controlled, and pick a slightly lighter weight than for a straight press.
Doing it seated with back support stops your torso from cheating.
hatalar: Rotating fast with heavy weight → Reduce the load and slow the rotation
Flaring the elbows fully out to the sides at the top → Keep your elbows in the scapular plane

ipuclari: One end of the bar in a corner or landmine holder; hold the other end in front of your shoulder.
Press diagonally up; your arm doesn't go fully overhead, so it's easier on the shoulder.
Can be done half-kneeling or standing; don't let your torso rotate.
At the top, reach your shoulder blade forward.
hatalar: Rotating the torso to press → Squeeze your glutes and bring the opposite hip forward
